prompt:
Research the officially documented limits of Cloudflare Workers on the free plan (requests per day, CPU time per request). Cite Cloudflare's own documentation and quote the limits.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
# Cloudflare Workers Free Plan Limits

Based on Cloudflare's official documentation, here are the documented limits for the Workers Free plan:

## Requests Per Day

SOURCE: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/ | QUOTE: "Accounts on the Workers Free plan have a daily request limit of 100,000 requests, resetting at midnight UTC." | CLAIM: The Workers Free plan allows 100,000 requests per day.

## CPU Time Per Request

SOURCE: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/pricing/ | QUOTE: "10 milliseconds of CPU time per invocation" | CLAIM: The Workers Free plan includes 10 milliseconds of CPU time per invocation/request.

SOURCE: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/ | QUOTE: "CPU time per HTTP request 10 ms" | CLAIM: The Workers Free plan has a CPU time limit of 10 ms per HTTP request.

## Additional Context

The limits documentation also clarifies what CPU time means and how it compares to real-world usage:

SOURCE: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/ | QUOTE: "The average Worker uses approximately 2.2 ms per request. Heavier workloads that handle authentication, server-side rendering, or parse large payloads typically use 10-20 ms." | CLAIM: The 10 ms CPU time limit on the Free plan is sufficient for average workloads but may be tight for heavier operations.

SOURCE: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/ | QUOTE: "Waiting on network requests (such as fetch() calls, KV reads, or database queries) does not count toward CPU time." | CLAIM: I/O wait time is excluded from the CPU time limit, meaning the 10 ms limit only applies to actual computation.
